messages:
sarah: FYI customer `ACME` (dedicated) reports embeddings endpoint suddenly spiking p95->2.5s, p99 ~5s. Only for bulk workload. They say they use dynamic batching with max_batch_size=64. Also got a handful of dimension-mismatch 413s earlier. Escalating.

raj: Can you drop a minimal repro + any server batching traces? Need to know if batches are overshooting max or there is queuing pressure.

sarah: Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":[<200 short strings>],"max_batch_size":64}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
```
Payload dims: 200 requests of length ~32 tokens each.
Server trace snippet (from /var/log/redwood/serving.log):
```
[2026-02-28T09:12:34Z] batch_enqueue: batch_id=abc123 queued=80 max_batch=64
[2026-02-28T09:12:34Z] dispatch_delay_ms=1820 actual_batch_size=70
[2026-02-28T09:12:34Z] worker_start batch_id=abc123
[2026-02-28T09:12:36Z] error client=acme status=413 dims=768
```
Looks like queue_time sometimes hits ~1.8s then large batch gets dispatched and we hit tail latency.

maria: A couple quick checks: 1) confirm client SDK version (old SDKs sometimes set client-side batching that conflicts with server settings), 2) check for auth refresh/retries (rotating tokens can cause duplicate bursts), 3) check multi-tenant coalescing config (are we coalescing across tenants for dedicated?).

sarah: Client uses internal wrapper around official SDK pinned to v0.9. They said they rotated tokens twice in short window -> might cause doubled requests.

raj: Can you enable batch debug headers and paste a single request trace? Use header `X-Redwood-Debug: batching` to get batch metadata. Also capture p50/p95/p99 histograms.

sarah: Pasting anonymized batch trace (header output):
```
batch_id=abc123; queued_at=09:12:33.200; dispatched_at=09:12:35.020; queue_time_ms=1820; actual_batch_size=70; split=none
batch_id=abc124; queued_at=09:12:33.400; dispatched_at=09:12:33.920; queue_time_ms=520; actual_batch_size=32
```
We see intermittently large queue times and actual_batch_size > configured max (70 vs 64) — looks like coalescing ignored max or the server slices after dispatch which still allows the worker to receive >max due to in-flight merge.

support-bot: Suggested temporary mitigations: 1) set customer max_batch_size=32, 2) disable dynamic batching (falls back to immediate dispatch), 3) enable fallback to smaller model variant to reduce compute latency. Also opened billing watch: repeated retries caused a spike in usage; recommend flagging for potential credit while we investigate. :eyes:

maria: Also check audit logs for token rotations (auth noise). Example query: `redwood audit list --principal acme --since 2026-02-28T09:00:00Z --filter event:token.rotate`

sarah: Ran that — found 2 rotate events within 30s of the spike window. Likely client retried with new token and old inflight requests combined, causing batch bundles to swell.

raj: Long term fix ideas: enforce strict max_batch at enqueue time (reject/dispatch early if queue size >= max_batch_size) and add a slice-split before worker dispatch to guarantee worker never sees >max. Also add telemetry to surface inter-tenant coalescing rates. I'll open a PR to do the split dispatch as a stopgap.

eng-ops-bot: Created incident INC-2026-042 (embeddings-batching-tail-latency). Assigned to @raj and @sarah. Slack thread linked.

sarah: Actions taken: set customer override max_batch_size=32, disabled dynamic batching for their tenant, notified customer about mitigations and billing watch. Will follow up with PR link once raj opens it.

raj: Please upload p99 histogram and the redwood runtime trace when available. We'll aim to ship split-dispatch hotfix in next sprint if tests pass.

support-bot: Customer updated: latency improved to p95 ~180ms after mitigations. Billing watch active. Closing escalation if no regressions in 24h. :white_check_mark:
